decisions.reason: The zero-based approximation leaves 1/0 undefined. This is a local indexing error: replace the error by 1/(n+1), n>=0. The finite-union supremum proof is otherwise valid, so no missing theorem or changed claim is involved. A1 also understated the existing AC use: RN versions are selected for every parameter, possibly uncountably many.

F5 cited a definition of a Dirac set function as if it already proved the probability-measure property. The missing justification is elementary and local: an empty event has value zero, total mass is one, and a disjoint family contains the chosen point at most once. Step 1.1 now supplies it and the exact conditional identity. F2 is also corrected to finite sets with full sigma-fields; arbitrary finite measurable spaces need not be standard Borel.

The instruction to assign an arbitrary conditional law on the sample-space complement is ill-typed: K is indexed by quotient classes, and the assigned off-support class already has a positive-mass row. The normalized class rows in the preceding sentence already give the correct complete kernel. Remove the extraneous assignment and explicitly retain that existing row off support; the sufficiency and atom comparison arguments need no new mathematical ingredient.

Singleton fibers and a trivial common-null ideal do not alone prove minimal sufficiency: a constant partition is coarser. The proof separately invokes the valid vector theorem F1, which already proves the claimed minimality, so the defect is an extraneous invalid inference rather than an unsupported final conclusion. Step 2.1 now checks all theorem hypotheses and uses F1 for minimality, reserving singleton fibers for injectivity and the null ideal for exactness of the comparison.

reviews.reason: The finite measure lambda is equivalent to mu and has total mass at most one; RN applies with the constant finite exhaustion. The corrected finite-subfamily approximations attain the finite supremum in a countable union A. Adding any remaining support cannot increase its measure, so all densities vanish off A almost everywhere. Positive mixture weights give Q-null => P_theta-null without combining uncountably many exceptional sets. AC remains explicit; the Statement is unchanged.

The explicit kernel has everywhere probability sections by a local disjoint-union proof and measurable evaluations on the finite discrete target. Its finite-sum conditional identity holds for every theta, A and C. Uniform R has no nonempty null sets, and the derivative is positive on u=0 but zero on u=1 within each T-fiber for every theta in (0,1), so no measurable version exists. The refuted implication and all dependencies remain unchanged.

Each class has positive finite normalizer and a parameter-independent probability row, now defined on every event. Off-support points use their assigned class row, while all P_theta ignore those points. Summing P_theta(A intersect D)=P_theta(D)K(D,A) proves sufficiency. For arbitrary sufficient H, AC selects countably many separating events; measurable H-atoms and common singleton conditional expectations force each atom's positive-support portion into one likelihood class. Countable atom unions give containment modulo the support complement, including all sufficient sigma-fields. Statement unchanged.

For Q({j})=2^(-j), f_k(j)=2^k 1_{j=k} integrates to delta_k on every discrete event and is finite and measurable. The sample space is standard Borel by its complete separable discrete metric, positive geometric weights sum to one, AC is explicit, and Q has no nonempty null set. F1 therefore supplies full minimal sufficiency against arbitrary sufficient sigma-fields, as verified in its Proof 4.1. Distinct nonzero-coordinate positions prove injectivity; the common-null ideal only makes the minimality inclusion exact. Example unchanged.
